**Cause:** `run_nightly_job` in `src/orders-service-v1/nightly_job.py` counted every payment whose `order_id` was missing from the order set. A retry repeats the payment with the same `id`, so each copy was counted.

**Fix:** The job now collects the ids of unmatched payments into a set and returns its size. Each payment id is counted once.

**Test:** I added `test_bank_retry_with_same_payment_id_is_counted_once` to `tests/test_orders_service_v1.py`. Before the fix it failed with `AssertionError: 2 != 1`. After the fix all 9 tests pass under `python3 -m unittest`.

- Verified: the new test fails before the fix (`2 != 1`) and passes after it. Full suite: 9 tests, OK.

- Inferred: the count is meant to be distinct unmatched payment ids. Nothing in the repo states that, but it is the only reading that fixes the retry case.
- Inferred: no other part of the system depends on the old double-counting. I only read the files in this repo.
